checks: Positive vertex heights and affineness give h_p=Σθ_jh_j and a uniform positive lower bound on the compact row hull. The algebraic identity 1−a·z′=h_p/h(z) proves the stated inverse; tilting convex-combination weights by positive h preserves segments in both directions.

After division by h(z), the original margin is b·z′+u·x′+(b·p−c)(1−a·z′)/h_p. This proves exact sign, including strict residual inequalities. At fixed base the continuous map is a scalar dilation, hence the q-dimensional Hausdorff scaling is exactly h(z)^{−q}.

The weights η_j=θ_jh_j/h_p sum to one and have mean zero in the new base. The original same-cap residuals satisfy the stated Minkowski inclusion because all strict inequalities are linear. Every positive finite q-measure destination is a q-dimensional convex set, and the directions of its positive Minkowski sum span the sum of the directions. Containment in the q-dimensional source forces them to agree.

Brunn–Minkowski on the common q-space, applied to closures of the positive convex residuals, gives Σθ_j|R_j|^{1/q}≤h_p. Substituting η_j and r_j gives the claimed root average. The separate volume identity retains h_j^{q−1} and is an algebraic equality, not an implication replacing the root moment.

The positive support-gap argument is valid: a convex threshold is bounded below by its affine support and above by the interpolation of the equal vertex values on the hull. Preserving the threshold mean in a row with a supporting affine function at p forces zero mean of the nonnegative support gaps. Original 374134af8a3f1b92 §1, (1)–(6), agrees.

overlap.comparison: Translate the row source to zero and set b=h_p. Its full projective chart proves the same inverse, affine cap map and intrinsic dilation law; its convex-weight rule gives η_j. The present result adds the common-direction argument and explicit positive strict-residual row root/volume pair for general intrinsic q and a supporting threshold face.

Taking no empty destination for one cap gives the full-dimensional unnormalized Brunn–Minkowski root inequality as its no-exit specialization. It does not give the intrinsic common-face chart or the companion volume moment.

review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The anchored chart and precise root/volume moment conversion are valid for positive intrinsic residuals on a common affine threshold face.
